items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 12:232:1
items.html: The third Ibur of the Mochin is called internality, and behold we have explained that the second Ibur is in externality, apart from the internality: Meaning, there are two aspects of the second Ibur: the first is after the two years of nursing, for the sake of the VAK of Gadlut; the second is after nine years and one day (as above, page 1159, item 102). And therefore the second Ibur that comes after the nine years, for the sake of the GAR of Gadlut, is called here the third Ibur of the Mochin. And he raises a difficulty: since only the third Ibur of the Mochin is called internality, but the second Ibur, that comes after the two years of nursing, is externality, as above — if so, how are the Mochin of the Shema called the aspect of internal, when they are only the aspect of the second Ibur of the VAK of the Mochin, and so it is externality? Now, according to what was explained above (item 175, the passage beginning “There is not”), that the Mochin of the Shema of Yotzer already belong to the Ibur that comes after the nine years, except that at the time of the Shema it receives only VAK from them — the above difficulty is well resolved. And see page 1188, item 185, which states explicitly that from this coupling of the Shema of Yotzer, all the internal Mochin of Gadlut and the surrounding lights of AVI enter ZA. Study it there well. But certainly it does not yet receive them all at once, but rather they enter it gradually, in their own way. For now, at the time of the Shema, it receives only the aspect of their Ibur and nursing, and afterward, in the Amida, it receives the remainder gradually, as is written in the Sefer HaKavanot.
